about: Which firmware version knows the flash chip of the newer FM-1 (the units with the M-VAVE logo on the front, sold from late 2026): UCUN UC25HQ80, JEDEC ID 0xB36014, instead of the Puya P25Q80H, 0x856014. Read by fm1companion/hardware.py; the rules are in docs/flash-protocol.md. Every row names where it was read. status: 'min' = from this version on the firmware accepts the chip (read in its source); 'none' = no released version accepts it; 'risky' = the code accepts the chip but it is not proven on one, or a unit did not start; 'documented' = no check in the firmware, other projects name it as the way back for these units; 'unverified' = nothing found. Nothing in this table was run on a newer FM-1 by FM-1 Companion.

melodee.source: firmware/src/project.c persist_boot (PR #111, issue #110); docs/RELEASE_1.6.0.md. In v1.6.0 and v1.6.1, in no release candidate of 1.6.0.
melodee.before: Every save failed and settings were lost.

skiff.source: release commit of 2.2: "Newer FM-1s with the UC25HQ80 flash save and update (#96)"

sloop.source: fm1_flash_id.h; README.md and SLOOP.md, note on 2.8.5
sloop.before: Projects stayed in RAM ("flash error") and the update loader refused to install.

karma.source: release commit "KARMA 3.0.4: steady with Ableton, and the new flash chip" (a SLOOP fork: FL_JEDEC_OK)
karma.before: As SLOOP before 2.8.5: nothing saved, the update loader refused to install.

jiant-fm.source: commit "V10.6z: accept the newer FM-1s' flash"; CHANGELOG.md V10.6z (2026-11-07); README.md
jiant-fm.before: The unit ran RAM-only: no saving, no Bluetooth segment, no updates.

felucca.source: "fix(flash): recognize UC25HQ80 in newer FM-1 units (fixes #320)"; README.md "Newer FM-1 flash"
felucca.before: 1.8.1 and earlier cannot start an update on such a unit (README); the way back is the official V15 through the chip's ROM boot.

choralroot-fm-1.source: hal/fm1_flash_map.h FL_JEDEC_OK; docs/HISTORY.md 3y222/3y223; docs/INSTALL-COMPAT.md "A second flash chip"; docs/releases/0.29.1.md
choralroot-fm-1.before: It ran RAM-only: nothing kept, "no unit ID", and every update was refused (the installers stop after 0 requests).

coralflower.source: commit "Support both known FM-1 flash chips" (first tag: v0.7)

x0x.source: firmware/hal/fm1_flash_ok.h (fm1-base#35); issue #46: 1.2.0 on a UC25HQ80 starts but cannot save or install
x0x.before: It starts, but cannot save and cannot install anything; the way out is its rescue script or the ROM boot.

fomni.before: Saves stayed in RAM and the update loader was never started.

amb-1.source: v1.3.1 pins fm1-base 9bca7154, which contains fm1-base e75b072 (device/fm1_flash_ok.h); firmware.json hardware.flash names B36014 from v1.3.1. v1.3 pins fm1-base 15dff6de (2026-10-17), without it.
amb-1.before: As fm1-base before e75b072: saves stayed in RAM and the update loader was never started.

loom-8.source: v0.13 pins fm1-base 698e2cba, which contains fm1-base e75b072; firmware.json hardware.flash names B36014 from v0.13. v0.12.1 pins fm1-base 2e96d846, without it.
loom-8.before: As fm1-base before e75b072: saves stayed in RAM and the update loader was never started.

hortator.source: tag drum-v1.0.1: "Flash: accept the UC25HQ80 (JEDEC 0xB36014) of newer FM-1s"
hortator.before: Saves stayed in RAM. (Its update loader has no check of the chip, according to that commit.)

transitfm1.before: 0.1.3 and earlier show UNKNOWN FLASH CHIP and refuse every install, the loader too; the way out is the ROM's USB boot.

orbit.source: firmware/hal/fm1_flash_map.h at 1dbb77d (2026-11-04, after v1.0.1B): FL_JEDEC_OK accepts only 0x856014 on the FM-1; project.c stays RAM-only otherwise and loader.c asks the same check
orbit.before: By its source: RAM-only, and its update loader does not accept the chip.

grimm.source: the fix exists only as commit f1b90ec (2026-11-08) on the branch v3, in no release; the latest release v2.0.2 (2026-11-03) does not have it

sloop3.source: its installer page (index.html, "Good to know"): "SLOOP 3 accepts this chip, but it has not been tried on one yet"; it needs m-bootloader, see there

m-bootloader.source: README.md "Little tested on the FM-1's newer flash chip": one such unit did not start after 1.1 or 1.2 was installed, cause not known; another runs 1.3 and 2.0 on one owner's report (M-Flasher #13); "install it at your own risk"

fm1-open.source: no statement and no check of the flash ID found in the repository (2026-10-21)

stock-v15.source: No source read says which original version the newer units ship with. Named as the way back on exactly these units by: Felucca README (1.8.2), ChoralRoot docs/releases/0.29.1.md and docs/INSTALL-COMPAT.md, TransitFM1 docs/SAFETY.md, MvaveFM1Unbricker (README and site, "New memory chip & Firmware Lock"). ChoralRoot HISTORY 3y222: such a unit took a firmware through M-VAVE's own updater from the original firmware it shipped with.

stock-v16.source: No source read says whether the V16 package (2026-10-21) was run on a newer unit, nor which version these units ship with.
